speaker: Doctor
text: I see you have neck and arm pain along with paresthesias and muscle weakness; to better understand the extent of nerve involvement, could you please tell me which specific fingers or areas of your arms are experiencing numbness or tingling?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old male. The patient reports a year-long history of burning pain in his neck and arms, accompanying paresthesias in his hands. Over the past 3 months, he has experienced increasing weakness in both hands. He has a history of type 2 diabetes mellitus, hypercholesterolemia, and hypertension. He was involved in a motor vehicle accident 3 years ago.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for the detailed history. Given your diabetes and the progressive nature of your symptoms, could you describe how the weakness in your hands is affecting your daily activities, such as buttoning shirts or holding objects? Additionally, have you noticed any changes in bladder or bowel control recently?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Burning pain in neck and arms, and weakness in both hands. I also have Paresthesias in hands, Absent reflexes, Decreased hand grip with fasciculations.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS).

I will now request MRI images of the cervical and thoracic spine to rule out compressive myelopathy before confirming this diagnosis. REQUEST IMAGES: Cervical_Spine_MRI and Thoracic_Spine_MRI.
